newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans up sharply on crop ratings, weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans up sharply on crop ratings, weather.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures were sharply higher in early trade, led by new crop on outlooks for hot, dry weather this weekend in the U.S. Midwest and on a lack of improvement in crop ratings, traders said.
Forecasts called for a mild week but temperatures were forecast to heat up this weekend with no significant moisture expected through August 6.

Traders also pointed to Monday's USDA weekly crop update which showed 62 percent of the soybean crop was rated good to excellent, unchanged from last week. The market had been looking for a one to two percent improvement.
Dry weather in portions of China's grain/soy growing region also was supportive, the traders said.

In opening trade, Rosenthal Collins, Cargill Investor Services and Merrill Lynch each bought one million bushels November, ADM bought 0.5 million November and O'Connor and Co bought 0.7 million November, pit sources said.
At 0955 CDT, soybeans were up 17-3/4 to 9-3/4 cents per bushel with November up 17-3/4 at $6.37 a bushel.
